name: Darmstadtium

discovery.discoverer: Peter Armbruster, Sigurd Hofmann and team, GSI Darmstadt

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced only via particle accelerator fusion, atom by atom.
majorUses: No practical applications — pure superheavy-element research
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive; observed only as individual atoms with sub-second half-lives.
notableCharacteristics: Named after Darmstadt, Germany, home of the GSI laboratory responsible for discovering it and several neighbouring superheavy elements.
ncertRelevance: named after a research lab's home city
whyHere: Predicted to sit in Group 10 below platinum and palladium, darmstadtium is expected to show broadly similar noble-metal-like chemistry, though this remains largely theoretical given how few atoms have ever been produced.
didYouKnow: GSI Darmstadt has been so productive at creating superheavy elements that it has multiple elements named directly or indirectly after its own city and researchers — darmstadtium being the most literal example.
genZNote: One German lab basically has a whole neighbourhood of the periodic table named after it and its scientists at this point.
